I'm pretty sure it isn't as easy to "leave" the United States as a lot of people pretend it is. Going through the trouble and cost of renunciation for most is going to cost them far more than had they just toughed out the next Presidency. If you don't renounce citizenship you are still expected to pay into the tax system while abroad. So most of these people would still be on the hook financially for choices made in a country AND they no longer live there. Not to mention those individuals or families will also owe taxes in the new country that they move to on top of it.
If someone does decide to renounce their citizenship they can expect to pay hundreds of thousands of dollars or more per family member in order to do so by the end of the process. When someone renounces their citizenship they are still obligated to pay an "Exit Tax" to the United States Government. This "Exit Tax" is typically hundreds of thousands of dollars or more per person alone and typically means that even if you renounce and move you will never truly be free from owing the US Government money. The cost for going into the embassy and renouncing citizenship is around $2,500.00 per person up from around approximately $450 previously. Once someone takes the oath of Renunciation, they turn in their passport and can expect to pay an "Intimidate Tax". The dumbed down way to look at how this tax is calculated would be to basically take account of the person(s) salary,home(s), retirement, savings, artwork, jewelry and stocks that they have amassed. Then based on the current market value of their total holdings they are provided with a tax figure owed to the government as if all of their holdings had just been sold.
So basically, unless an individual or family has the amount to buy out up front they will be taxed on that amount until it is paid off. On top of it all once they take the oath of renunciation all rights granted to an individual as a United States Citizen are immediately stripped however, said tax is still owed regardless. Individuals complaining about leaving the country during election years has all but become common place. In the end though, it is a lot harder than a lot of folks realize and once it's all said and done, that does not guarantee that individual(s) a better more prosperous life. We may not be perfect in this country but compared to a large portion of the world we are still the most perfect country IMO.
It seems like a lot of people these days are looking for someone or something to create the change they want to see in this world. There is an inherent part of human rationalization that creates this mindset and if we teach ourselves to approach a lot of the problems we encounter with a different mindset it would be amazing what we could accomplish.
The best way to demonstrate this is with a story that I often tell to newer manager trainees and team leaders we are trying to develop in our own company.
In the story we tell about a man who wanted to change the world. He would wake up daily disgusted with the things he was seeing and hearing in the news and in the way he saw how things were being run. He finally had enough and decided to set out and do something about it. He spent half of his life traveling the globe. During his travels he would constantly tell everyone what they were doing was wrong and point out the problems. He would travel from city to city, state to state, country to country trying to tell them how they were wrong and how things should be.
Over time he began to realize that the people were not doing what he had said and he had made almost no progress in changing anything yet alone the world. The man decided perhaps the world was too big of a target to change and he would need to narrow his sights.
What the man needed to do was change his country! The man understood his country and the countries problems better than anyone and he knew he was going to make it happen this time. The man spent the next 10 years traveling his country telling people what was wrong and explaining to them that he had the plans to fix it all and they had to listen to him. After his 10 years of travels came to an end he had realized he still made little to no impact on his goal of changing his country... The man undeterred, decided it was time to again narrow his sights and focus on his community. He spent an additional few years around his home town trying to impact the way they functioned and trying to get them to follow his lead. Yet, even with all his years of effort pointing out what needed to change, the community still did not change. The man too exhausted from years of travels and countless days and hours of pointing out the problems the man decided he could muster only enough strength to try and at least straighten out his own family. He would tell his kids what they were doing wrong from raising their own children to the financial choices they made.
Eventually the old man found himself on his deathbed, a life spent trying to change a climate that seemingly did not welcome his feedback. It was at this moment surrounded by crying family and friends that the old man realized something. Had the man simply started by changing himself and focusing on his own opportunities first, through his actions he could have changed his family. That family in turn could have gone on to change the community which could have impacted the country which would have changed the world.
Often times in life we look at problems backwards and we have to just simply realize, if we exemplify the change we want to see by our own actions, we often will have a much larger impact on our surroundings than just pointing out other peoples mistakes and telling them what is right or wrong.
